messages:
morgan: heads up — eu-west started spiking on per-GPU tail latency, autoscaler trimmed a couple slices on shared-gpu. infra-bot posted the alert.
infra-bot: ALERT 2712345678 region=eu-west metric=gpu_tail_99.9=852ms threshold=800ms (affected pool=shared-gpu/pool-24)
kai: which tenants? any heavy kv-cache hitters?
morgan: looks like tenant-alpha bursty long-context runs, also some rerank jobs. logs: `kvcache_evictions/sec` doubled for the pool in the last 6m.
sasha: tenant-alpha is on soft-affinity. pattern repeats ~6h. i'm thinking we should trial a small "hedge" reserve topology in eu-west to absorb short low-cost requests and protect shared slices from noise.
devon: cost check — 10% reserve of the region is how many GPUs? rough calc: eu-west capacity ~40 GPUs -> 4 GPUs reserve. cost ~4 * $3.2/hr ~= $12.8/hr. cheaper than increased tail latency impact for SLA customers, but want to confirm options (pre-warm vs on-demand warm).
morgan: i ran a quick probe: `curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/metrics?region=eu-west&pool=shared-gpu" | jq '.[] | {ts, gpu_tail_99.9, kvcache_evictions}' | tail -n 20` — shows sustained tail rise aligned with tenant-alpha bursts.
sasha: proposed routing snippet (canary):
```
route_policy:
  name: hedge-euw-v1
  match: request.pred_latency < 50ms && request.seq_len < 2048
  route: reserve-hedge-pool
  fallback: shared-gpu/pool-24
  capacity_reserve: 10%
  rollout: ramp 1% every 2m
```
kai: if we route small fast requests to reserve pool, we need to ensure model variant parity (quantization + kvcache warm). otherwise we risk QoE regressions when fallback happens.
devon: agree. can we restrict hedge to a compatible model bin (like -q4 and same kv schema)? that keeps runtime parity and reduces cold-warm mismatch.
sasha: yep — limit to model-224q4 and only for requests without function-calls. also will pin `kvcache_prefetch: true` in reserve config so warmup is instant-ish.

morgan: what's the plan for rollout observability? i'd like token-level cost, tail-latency p99.9 for reserve vs shared, and a synthetic hit test every 30s.
kai: add new alert: `reserve_p99.9 > shared_p99.9 * 1.5` and `fallback_rate > 0.5%` within 10m -> rollback. also emit per-tenant fallback_count metric.

sasha: schedule: canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC — single AZ (eu-west-2a), 4 GPUs reserved, ramp policy as above, monitor for 30m then expand to 2 AZs if stable.
devon: cost-team FYI @cost-team — we'll run ~4 GPUs for canary (expected ~12.8/hr). flag if that bumps monthly projection too much.

oncall-lagoon: :eyes: i'll be watching pogos and ready to rollback. remind me which runbook to follow if fallback spikes? (looking for links)
morgan: runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/hedge-reserve-rollback — steps 1-5. rollback = set rollout to 0 and drain reserve pool, then restore traffic to shared.

kai: minor nit — ensure autoscaler windows don't think reserve is free headroom. add `autoscaler.ignore_label: reserve-hedge` so it doesn't steal capacity.
sasha: good catch. will patch controller config and push canary manifest now. patch diff:
```
- labels:
-  role: worker
+ labels:
+  role: worker
+  reserve: hedge-euw-v1
+ autoscaler-ignore: "true"
```

infra-bot: SCHEDULE 2712345678-canary-action scheduled at 2026-03-21T03:00:00Z (action=deploy-reserve-hedge eu-west-2a, capacity=4 GPUs, rollout=ramp 1%/2m)
morgan: thanks — please capture tenant-alpha traffic trace and fallback counts. post a short summary after 60m. :thumbsup:
kai: will also add a quick synthetic that exercises the kvcache warm path and measures cold->warm latency delta.
sasha: i'll open a short dashboard for the canary with cost, p99.9, fallback_rate, and kvcache_evictions. will DM links when ready.
devon: acked. if cost-team flags, we can shorten canary to 20m or reduce to 2 GPUs. want to keep cheaper rollback options.
oncall-lagoon: standing by. if anything looks off i'll flip rollout to 0 and drain, no drama.
morgan: final call — proceed with canary tomorrow. we'll reconvene in #eng-sre after 30m of canary data. thanks y'all.
